title: YOURLS
name: yourls
description: URL shortener you run yourself: short links on your own address with custom keywords, click stats with referrers and countries, bookmarklets and an API for making links from scripts. Source: https://github.com/YOURLS/YOURLS

env.name: YOURLS_URL
env.label: Address you'll open it on (required)
env.description: Exactly what you'll type in the browser, port included, all lowercase and no slash at the end, like http://192.168.1.20:8400. Every short link and admin page is built from it.

env.name: YOURLS_ADMIN_PASSWORD
env.label: Admin password (required)
env.description: What you'll log in to the admin area with.

env.name: YOURLS_COOKIE_KEY
env.label: Cookie key
env.description: Keeps you logged in, and your API signature token the same, across updates. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32. Left blank, both change every time it's updated.

note: Fill in the address, admin password and database password before you deploy, since the stack won't start without them. The address has to be exactly what you'll type in the browser, like http://192.168.1.20:8400: the port you're using, all lowercase, and no slash at the end. YOURLS builds every short link, page and button from it, so if it's wrong /admin sends you off to that address to install, any page you do reach has no styling and won't shorten anything, and short links point at the wrong place. To fix it, change the address in the stack's environment variables and redeploy. Then open /admin on that address (the bare address just says Forbidden, that's normal), click Install YOURLS once to set up the database, and log in with the admin username and password from the form. The login lives in the stack's environment variables, so that's where you change the password. The install adds three sample links to yourls.org, delete them if you like. Short links are public, and so are their stats pages (add a + to any short link), which load their charts and site icons from Google. For scripts, use the signature token under Tools rather than your password, and set a cookie key so the token survives updates. Links and stats live in the db-data volume. Docs: yourls.org/docs
